messages:
anna: FYI discovered a prio vuln in our alpine base images — OpenSSL CVE-ish causing TLS client failures in some infra paths. thinking about a hotpatch + image promotion rather than full rebuild to move faster. any blockers for signing/promotion? :eyes:

devon: hotpatch ok as short-term. question: will the image signer (KMS) accept a hotpatched layer? we usually sign the final tarball with key1. if we rebuild we rotate to key2 per policy.

maria: Signing policy requires key usage audit entries and `image:promote` RBAC role. if we reuse key1 we need explicit exec approval and an audit note. pinging @devon — do you have the `image:promote` role in the signer service account?

devon: i don't. i'm on `image:build` + `image:canary` only. i'll need a short-lived grant or a service account flow. @maria can we use delegated signing via ephemeral creds?

maria: yes — we can grant `image:promote` for 1 hour via the RBAC admin flow. but we must capture an audit log entry that includes the CVE ID and root cause. that goes to the compliance bucket.

anna: that's fine. also notes for QA: the hotpatch will change /usr/lib/libssl.so ABI minor symlink on some tags; need canary with both x86 and arm builds. keep canary traffic to 2% for 24h.

jon: for canary image names, let's tag `redwood/base:alpine-3.18-openssl-hotpatch-<sha>` and keep original `alpine-3.18-openssl-<sha>` until promoted. build command for reproducibility: 

```
# build + push
docker build -f docker/alpine/Dockerfile -t registry.redwood.com/redwood/base:alpine-3.18-openssl-hotpatch-${GIT_SHA} .
docker push registry.redwood.com/redwood/base:alpine-3.18-openssl-hotpatch-${GIT_SHA}
```

jon: also we'll attach SBOM and note `reproducible: false (hotpatch)` in the metadata.

devon: KMS questions: when signing, do we create a new `image-signature` entry with `key: key1` and annotate `patch=true`? we need to ensure old signatures remain valid for rollback.

maria: yes annotate `patch=true` and include `cve: CVE-2026-XXXX` + `changelist: hotpatch-layer-123`. Audit log must contain the approval ticket ID.

anna: can we automate the ephemeral RBAC grant + audit entry as part of the CI job? manual approvals slow us down.

maria: we can. plan: 1) create a CI step that requests an ephemeral grant from RBAC service 2) RBAC returns token and logs request 3) operator approves in UI (1 click) 4) CI proceeds and attaches the approval id to the signature. will need an IAC change in `infra/rbac/policies`.

devon: sounds good. what about KMS key rotation rules? do we need to rotate before signing hotpatch?

maria: not required for an emergency hotpatch. but we must record key id and current key rotation window. we'll add `key_id:key1; key_rotation_due:2026-09-01` to the signature metadata. ops: if key1 gets revoked, the promotion path must fail-safe.

anna: QA checklist: 1) smoke + TLS handshake tests to critical upstreams 2) internal api e2e with header tracing 3) memory/regression quick tests 4) canary traffic 2% x24h 5) promote if no errors.

jon: adding the test command snippet for handshake smoke: 

```
openssl s_client -connect api.internal.redwood.com:443 -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
```

anna: deploy-bot will create canary. please add `--dry-run` tag for first push so we can validate metadata before real promotion.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Created canary image registry.redwood.com/redwood/base:alpine-3.18-openssl-hotpatch-2005567890 (dry-run). Canary traffic set to 0% until approval. :robot_face:

devon: I'll request ephemeral `image:promote` grant now and attach ticket SEC-1223.

maria: once grant is live, CI will sign with KMS and write audit entry. i'll watch the audit stream and post link.

anna: thanks. after QA and stable 24h canary we'll finalize promotion process and schedule a scheduled rebuild (full rebase) next sprint to remove hotpatch technical debt.

devon: noted. i'll also run local apk upgrade in a container and capture `ldd` diffs for libc/ssl to ensure no ABI surprises.

anna: perfect. leaving this open for any blocking ops. :thumbsup:

maria: filing a follow-up doc in the security runbook with steps + sample audit payloads. will ping here when done.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary readiness check passed (metadata validated). awaiting signature + approval.
